summary: The bill amends federal criminal law to prohibit providing or attempting a chemical abortion (using mifepristone, misoprostol, or similar drugs) in or affecting interstate commerce unless a healthcare provider physically examines the patient, is present at the abortion site, and supplies a catch kit plus red-bag biohazard waste container for proper disposal, with penalties of up to 5 years in prison and a $50,000 fine per violation.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures. It is a criminal prohibition on certain abortion practices.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.

While the bill regulates how chemical abortions may be provided, it does not address the structure of healthcare coverage, public vs. private systems, insurance mandates, or market-based reforms. The impact on the defined spectrum is negligible.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No immigration, border, or visa-related content exists in the bill.

The bill amends federal criminal law to prohibit chemical (medication) abortions unless a healthcare provider is physically present, performs an in-person examination, and follows specific medical-waste protocols. Violations carry up to five years imprisonment and fines. This directly restricts access to medication abortion by banning remote/telehealth provision and imposing new procedural requirements, thereby pushing strongly toward the restrict-access end of the spectrum.
No defense, military, or national-security spending or policy provisions are present.
The short title references 'Clean Water,' but the operative text concerns abortion regulation only; no environmental, regulatory, or climate provisions exist.
The bill does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social-safety-net eligibility or funding.
No education funding, school-choice, or federal-education-policy content is included.
Although the bill defines 'chemical abortion drug,' it does so solely to regulate abortion access and does not address broader drug decriminalization, legalization, or enforcement policy.

The bill creates a new federal criminal offense with penalties, but this is narrowly tailored to abortion procedures rather than general sentencing reform, rehabilitation, or policing policy. The effect on the broader criminal-justice spectrum is incidental.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
The bill has no fiscal, deficit, or debt-reduction implications.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
The legislation contains no foreign-aid authorizations or restrictions.
No voting-access, election-integrity, or campaign-related measures are included.
The bill does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or digital surveillance.
No labor, union, or workplace-regulation content exists.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, conscience protections, or conflicts between civil-rights laws and religious liberty.
